newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy April bank deposits fall but loans rise-ABI.
newsitem.headline: Italy April bank deposits fall but loans rise-ABI.

text.p: Deposits in the Italian banking system fell in April while loans rose only slightly, the Italian Banking Association (ABI) said in its latest monthly report.

Total loans by banks holding short-term deposits, accounting for all high street banks, rose just 4.67 percent year-on-year in April to 892.10 trillion lire, above a 4.21 percent rise in March but below February's 4.68 percent increase.

Lira loans rose by only 4.38 percent to 807.10 trillion lire after a 4.37 percent rise in March. But foreign currency loans jumped 7.51 percent to 85.0 trillion lire after a March increase of just 2.77 percent.
However, ABI said deposits slipped 0.5 percent year-on-year in April to 864.00 trillion lire, the first fall seen since August 1995, after a rise of 1.49 percent in March.
ABI noted that available data for the first part of this year showed "a persisting weakness in financing demand."
On bad loans, latest data for January showed that the rate of growth of bad loans in the Italian banking system fell that month, mainly due to accounting adjustments, ABI said.
Bad loans rose by just 3.4 percent year-on-year in January to 114.66 trillion lire, but net of adjustments for problem loans rose 11.5 percent after an 11.6 percent December rise.
The ratio of bad loans to total loans fell to 10.42 percent in January, but rose to 11.30 percent net of adjustments, after a ratio of 11.28 percent in December.
